answer: Agents exchanging walnut, yarrow and vine crop models defend collaborative training with a trusted reference gradient computed on independently collected farm data. Each submitted update is clipped, then assigned weight only for positive alignment with that reference; weights are normalized before aggregation. A swarm of aliases sending opposite gradients gets zero weight regardless of its size. This limits directional model poisoning, not all sybil attacks: biased reference data or malicious aligned updates remain weaknesses.
